meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT solutions for Class 12 Maths Exercise 1.2 on one-one, onto and bijective functions, plus a free 8-question quiz to test yourself.

quiz.title: Types of Functions Quiz (Ex 1.2)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on one-one (injective), onto (surjective) and bijective functions, drawn straight from Exercise 1.2. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Relations and Functions, Exercise 1.2 (types of functions)

questions.q: A function f : A → B is called one-one (injective) when:
options: Every element of B has a pre-image
Distinct elements of A have distinct images in B
f(a) is the same for all a
A and B have equal size
questions.explanation: Injective means f(x₁) = f(x₂) forces x₁ = x₂ — distinct inputs never share an image.

questions.q: A function f : A → B is onto (surjective) when:
options: Its range equals its co-domain B
No two inputs share an image
questions.explanation: Surjective means every element of the co-domain B is an image of some element of A, so range = co-domain.

questions.q: The function f : N → N given by f(x) = 2x is:
questions.explanation: Different naturals give different doubles (one-one), but odd numbers like 3 are never hit, so it is not onto N.

questions.q: For f : R → R, f(x) = x² is:
questions.explanation: f(−2) = f(2) = 4 breaks one-one, and negative numbers have no square-root pre-image, so it is not onto R either.

questions.q: A function that is both one-one and onto is called:
questions.explanation: A bijection is injective and surjective together, which is exactly the condition for an inverse to exist.

questions.q: How many one-one functions are there from a set with 2 elements to a set with 3 elements?
questions.explanation: The first element has 3 image choices, the second has 2 remaining: 3 × 2 = 6.

questions.q: The signum function f : R → R (giving −1, 0 or 1) is:
questions.explanation: Many inputs map to 1 (not one-one) and its range is only {−1, 0, 1}, not all of R (not onto).

questions.q: If A has 3 elements and B has 3 elements, a one-one function f : A → B is automatically:
questions.explanation: For finite sets of equal size, a one-one function uses all 3 distinct images, so it is also onto — and therefore bijective.

faq.q: What is the difference between one-one and onto functions?
faq.a: A one-one (injective) function sends distinct inputs to distinct outputs, so f(x₁) = f(x₂) implies x₁ = x₂. An onto (surjective) function covers the whole co-domain, meaning every element of B is the image of at least one element of A. A function can be one but not the other.

faq.q: How do I prove a function is one-one in Exercise 1.2?
faq.a: Assume f(x₁) = f(x₂), then use algebra to show x₁ = x₂. For a graph, apply the horizontal-line test: if no horizontal line meets the graph more than once, the function is one-one.

faq.q: How do I check whether a function is onto?
faq.a: Take an arbitrary element y in the co-domain and try to solve f(x) = y for some x in the domain. If a valid x always exists, the function is onto; if some y has no pre-image, it is not. In short, onto means range equals co-domain.
A function is bijective when it is both one-one and onto. Only bijective functions are invertible, which is why Exercise 1.2 matters before you study inverse functions later in the chapter.
